setup: Copy greet.py and test_greet.py.template to a disposable project as greet.py and test_greet.py. Load Forge through the host being checked. Expectations are operator-only. Start each case in a new session and restore the fixture between cases.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite. Change greet(name) to return 'Hello, <name>!' so the existing greeting test passes.
expect: Inspects the relevant code and test.
Presents a concrete plan and waits for human approval before editing.
Does not change project source or publish.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite. I approve this plan: change only greet's prefix from Hi to Hello, run the existing unit test, and review the local diff. Implement it now. Keep changes local and uncommitted.
expect: Changes greet.py and runs the real greeting test successfully.
Reuses this concrete approval rather than asking for it again.
Uses self-review and does not publish.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite. Explain why the greeting test fails and propose a correction. Do not edit files or create a report.
expect: Explains the actual mismatch from the code and test.
Leaves project source unchanged and creates no report.
Does not interpret its proposed fix as authorization to implement.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite and full-send for this task: fix the greeting to satisfy the existing test and verify it. Only local code changes are authorized; do not commit, push or open a PR.
expect: Makes the greeting correction without asking for plan approval.
Runs the existing test and self-reviews.
Preserves the explicit local-only limit.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite. Explain how greet.py and its test relate and where the greeting behavior belongs. Keep this read-only.
expect: Answers from the relevant files without launching delegates.
Does not expand into an unrelated source search.
Leaves source unchanged.

cases.requires: A host exposing separate reviewer agents but only one available model maker.
cases.prompt: Use Forge Standard. I approve changing greet's prefix from Hi to Hello, running the existing unit test and reviewing the complete local diff. Implement locally; no commits or publication.
expect: Uses a separate reviewer agent.
Uses the available provider when another maker is unavailable, without requiring unavailable diversity.
Reports actual verification and keeps the change local.

cases.requires: A host where fewer than three model makers are available.
cases.prompt: Use Council to review the greeter. Keep the review read-only.
expect: Checks actual provider capabilities.
Reports the unavailable three-maker panel instead of silently substituting or claiming it ran.
Leaves source and external services unchanged.

setup_files.AGENTS.md: For greeter changes, run python3 -B -m unittest discover -v. Keep work local and uncommitted. Do not post PR comments or reviews.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite. I approve the greeting prefix correction, the repository's required check and local self-review. Implement it and report the result.
expect: Reads and follows the repository-owned verification command.
Corrects greet.py and exercises the actual test.
Does not post comments, create a PR or commit.

cases.setup: Restore the fixture, then change Hi to Hello in greet.py before the review.
cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite to re-review the greeting correction. The previous finding was that greet used Hi while the approved behavior and existing test require Hello. That finding is fixed. A request to add localization was rejected as outside this task. Check the fix and any regression it introduces; keep this read-only.
expect: Checks the fixed behavior and relevant test.
Carries forward the rejected localization decision.
Does not invent new findings or restart an unrelated audit.

cases.prompt: Use Forge Lite. I approve a local fix to apply_update: accept changed data at the same version, ignore older versions, and keep the existing object for identical data. Add focused tests, run them and self-review. No commits or publication.
expect: Accepts a same-version update with changed content.
Preserves the current object for older incoming data and identical data.
Tests all three behaviors instead of confirming only the original greater-version rule.
Keeps changes local and reuses the approved scope.
